parts.problemMd:
Two $24 Ω$ resistors are connected in series to a 12 V battery.

![Circuit diagram showing a 12 V battery connected in series to two 24 ohm resistors, forming a simple closed loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-science-combined-science-23-physics/electricity-magnetism/electric-circuits-safety/assets/005-circuit-diagram-showing-a-12-v-battery-connected.png)

What is the current in **one** of the resistors?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- In series, the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances

$R_{total} = 24 + 24 = 48 Ω$

- The same current flows through both resistors in a series circuit

$I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{48}$

$= 0 . 25 \text{A}$

**B** is incorrect because $0 . 50 \text{A} = \frac{12}{24}$, using the resistance of only one resistor instead of the total series resistance

**C** is incorrect because $2 . 0 \text{A} = \frac{48}{24}$, an incorrect combination of the values rather than $V \div R$

**D** is incorrect because $4 . 0 \text{A} = \frac{48}{12}$, inverting the equation ($R \div V$ instead of $V \div R$)

parts.solutionMd:

- In this circuit, all three LEDs (P, Q, and R) are connected in reverse bias, so no current flows through any of them and none are lit

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a 12 V battery connected to an ammeter and two $10 Ω$ resistors.

![Circuit diagram with 12 V battery, ammeter in series, and two 10 Ω resistors connected in parallel between the battery terminals.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-science-combined-science-23-physics/electricity-magnetism/electric-circuits-safety/assets/003-circuit-diagram-with-12-v-battery-ammeter-in-ser.png)

What is the reading on the ammeter?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The two 10 Ω resistors are in parallel, so the combined resistance is found using:

$\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{10}$

$R = 5 Ω$

- Current = voltage ÷ resistance

$I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{5}$

$= 2 . 4 \text{A}$

**A** is incorrect because $0 . 60 \text{A} = \frac{12}{20}$, treating the resistors as if they were in series (total resistance 20 Ω) instead of parallel

**B** is incorrect because $1 . 2 \text{A} = \frac{12}{10}$, using the resistance of only one resistor instead of the combined parallel resistance

**D** is incorrect because $60 \text{A} = \frac{12}{0.2}$, inverting the combined resistance (using 0.2 Ω instead of 5 Ω)

parts.problemMd:
Fig. 9.1 shows a circuit used in a toy car.

![Circuit diagram with cell P, switch Q, LED S, fixed resistor R, variable resistor T and motor U connected in series, forming a complete electrical circuit.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-science-combined-science-23-physics/electricity-magnetism/electric-circuits-safety/assets/001-circuit-diagram-with-cell-p-switch-q-led-s-fixed.png)

**Fig. 9.1**

(i) The resistance of component **T** is $5 . 4 Ω$. The resistance of component **U** is $3 . 5 Ω$.

Calculate the combined resistance of components T and U.

[1]

(ii) The current in component R is 2.7 A. The current in component T is 2.5 A.

Determine the current in component S and component U.

[2]

(iii) State the name of component S.

[1]
parts.solutionMd:
(i)

To calculate the combined resistance of components T and U:

$R_{TU} = 5 . 4 + 3 . 5$

$= 8 . 9 Ω$

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - $8 . 9 Ω$ **[1 mark]**

(ii)

Using Kirchhoff's current law at the junction, the current in component R splits between the branch containing S and the branch containing T and U:

$I_{S} = I_{R} - I_{T} = 2 . 7 - 2 . 5$

I<sub>S</sub> = **0.2 A**

Since T and U are in series, the current in U is the same as the current in T:

I<sub>U</sub> = **2.5 A**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - current in S = 0.2 A **[1 mark]**
> - current in U = 2.5 A **[1 mark]**

(iii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - LED / light-emitting diode **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> At a junction in a circuit, the total current flowing in must equal the total current flowing out (Kirchhoff's current law) — use this to find an unknown branch current when you know the others. Components connected in series (like T and U here) always carry the same current.

parts.problemMd:
A car of mass 800 kg is travelling in a straight line at a constant speed of 12 m/s. A constant resultant force then acts on the car causing the speed to increase.

After 5.0 s, the speed of the car is 20 m/s.

What is the size of the resultant force acting on the car?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time

$a = \frac{v-u}{t} = \frac{20-12}{5.0}$

$= 1 . 6 \text{m} / \text{s}^{2}$

- Force = mass × acceleration

$F = m a = 800 \times 1 . 6$

$= 1280 \text{N}$

parts.problemMd:

The object moves 3.0 m vertically upwards and 4.0 m horizontally.

How much work is done by the 200 N force?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force

$W = F \times d = 200 \times 5 . 0$

$= 1000 \text{J}$

- The distance used is the distance along the slope (5.0 m), not the vertical or horizontal component

**A** is incorrect because 600 J = 200 × 3.0, using the vertical distance instead of the distance along the slope

**B** is incorrect because 800 J = 200 × 4.0, using the horizontal distance instead of the distance along the slope

**D** is incorrect because 1400 J = 200 × 7.0, incorrectly adding the vertical and horizontal distances ($3 . 0 + 4 . 0$) instead of using the distance along the slope

parts.problemMd:
A solid block has a density of 1.1 g/cm<sup>3</sup>.

The block is lowered into three liquids, X, Y and Z, with different densities.

The densities of the liquids are:

liquid X: 1.0 g/cm<sup>3</sup>

liquid Y: 1.2 g/cm<sup>3</sup>

liquid Z: 1.3 g/cm<sup>3</sup>

In which of the liquids does the block float?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- An object floats when the liquid's density is greater than the object's density
- The block has a density of 1.1 g/cm<sup>3</sup>, so it floats only in liquids Y (1.2 g/cm<sup>3</sup>) and Z (1.3 g/cm<sup>3</sup>), which are both denser than the block
- It sinks in liquid X (1.0 g/cm<sup>3</sup>), which is less dense than the block

**A** is incorrect because the block also floats in liquid Z, since Z is denser than the block, not just Y

**C** is incorrect because the block sinks in liquid X, since X is less dense than the block

**D** is incorrect because the block floats in both Y and Z, but sinks in X, since X is less dense than the block

parts.problemMd:
The Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of $1 . 51 \times 10^{8} \text{km}$ and takes $365 . 25 \text{days}$ for one orbit.

Calculate the orbital speed of the Earth around the Sun in $\text{km/h}$.
parts.solutionMd:
To calculate the orbital speed of the Earth:

- List the known quantities:

- Radius of orbit, r = 1.51 × 10<sup>8</sup> km
- Time for one orbit, T = 365.25 days

- Convert the time to hours:

$T = 365 . 25 \times 24$ **[1 mark]**

$T = 8766 \text{h}$

- Write down the equation:

$v = \frac{2πr}{T}$

- Substitute the known values:

$v = \frac{2π\times1.51\times10^{8}}{8766}$ **[1 mark]**

- Calculate the answer:

v = **1.08 × 10**<sup>**5**</sup>** km/h** **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for correctly converting 365.25 days to 8766 hours
> 
> 1 mark for correct substitution into $v = \frac{2πr}{T}$ (accept formula in any form)
> 
> 1 mark for a correct final answer of 1.08 × 10<sup>5</sup> km/h

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always check the units required by the question — here the answer needs to be in km/h, so make sure you convert the orbital period from days into hours before substituting into the equation.

parts.problemMd:
A tank is full of a warm liquid. A student wants to place a cooling unit inside the tank to cool all the liquid as quickly as possible. There are two possible positions for the cooling unit, **P** and **Q**. The positions are shown in the diagram.

![Diagram of a vertical tank of warm liquid on a bench, showing possible cooling unit positions P near the top and Q near the bottom of the tank.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-science-combined-science-23-physics/thermal-physics/transfer-of-thermal-energy/assets/001-diagram-of-a-vertical-tank-of-warm-liquid-on-a-b.png)

How does cooling affect the density of the liquid and what is the best position for the cooling unit?

|   | effect of cooling | best position for cooling unit |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | decreases density | **P** |
| **B** | decreases density | **Q** |
| **C** | increases density | **P** |
| **D** | increases density | **Q** |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Cooling increases the density of the liquid
- Placing the cooling unit at position P (top) allows the cooled, denser liquid to sink while warmer, less dense liquid rises, creating a convection current that circulates and cools all the liquid

**A** is incorrect because although position P is correct, cooling decreases the density is wrong — cooling increases the density of the liquid

**B** is incorrect because both parts are wrong — cooling increases density (not decreases), and position P (not Q) is best since the denser cooled liquid needs to sink from the top

**D** is incorrect because although cooling increasing density is correct, position Q is wrong — the cooling unit should be at P so cooled, denser liquid sinks and creates a convection current

parts.problemMd:
(i) Thermal energy transfer from the Sun to the Earth is mainly due to radiation in one region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

State the name of this region.

[1]

(ii) Electromagnetic radiation from the Sun heats the Earth.

Circle the correct words or phrases to complete the paragraph.

The temperature of the Earth is increasing. This is because the amount of radiation absorbed / emitted by the Earth from the Sun is greater than / less than the amount of radiation absorbed / emitted by the Earth into space.

[1]
parts.solutionMd:
(i)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - infrared **[1 mark]**

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - absorbed AND greater than AND emitted **[1 mark]**
> - Marks must be awarded in this order

> **[exam-tip]**
> The Earth's temperature rises when it absorbs more radiation from the Sun than it emits back into space — this imbalance between absorbed and emitted radiation is the key idea behind the greenhouse effect.

parts.problemMd:
Solar power can also be used to generate electricity.

(i) Visible light from the Sun contains all the colours of the visible spectrum.

State the colour with the longest wavelength.

[1]

(ii) Most of the energy from the Sun is radiated in three regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

One of these regions is visible light.

State the name of one of the other two regions.

[1]
parts.solutionMd:
(i)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - red **[1 mark]**

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - infrared **OR** ultraviolet **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Remember the order of the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. Visible light sits in the middle, with infrared having a longer wavelength and ultraviolet a shorter one.

parts.problemMd:
A wave has a frequency of 6.0 kHz and travels at a speed of 300 m/s.

What is the wavelength of the wave?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- Wavelength = speed ÷ frequency

$λ = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{300}{6000}$

$= 0 . 050 \text{m}$

- Remember to convert 6.0 kHz to hertz: 6.0 kHz = 6000 Hz

parts.problemMd:
A seismic P-wave (primary) passes through the ground.

What is the nature of this wave and what is the direction of vibration of the ground as the P-wave passes through it?

|   | nature of P-wave | direction of vibration |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | longitudinal | at right angles to direction of propagation |
| **B** | longitudinal | parallel to direction of propagation |
| **C** | transverse | at right angles to direction of propagation |
| **D** | transverse | parallel to direction of propagation |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- P-waves are longitudinal waves
- The ground particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation (compressions and rarefactions in the same direction as the wave travels)

**A** is incorrect because although P-waves are correctly described as longitudinal, the direction of vibration is given as at right angles to propagation — it should be parallel

**C** is incorrect because P-waves are described as transverse, but they are longitudinal, and the direction of vibration given is also incorrect

**D** is incorrect because P-waves are described as transverse, but they are longitudinal, even though the direction of vibration (parallel) is correct

parts.problemMd:
Earthquakes produce seismic P-waves (primary) and seismic S-waves (secondary). P-waves are longitudinal and S-waves are transverse.

(i) State **one** other type of longitudinal wave.

[1]

(ii) Describe the difference between transverse waves and longitudinal waves.

[2]
parts.solutionMd:
(i)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - sound **[1 mark]**

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - transverse waves: the direction of vibration is at right angles to the direction of propagation **[1 mark]**
> - longitudinal waves: the direction of vibration is parallel to the direction of propagation **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> A quick way to remember the difference: in a transverse wave the vibrations are perpendicular ("across") the direction of travel, like a wave on a rope; in a longitudinal wave the vibrations are parallel ("along") the direction of travel, like sound waves.

parts.problemMd:
White light passes through a glass prism and produces a spectrum.

Which diagram shows the paths of the red light and the violet light?

![Four labelled glass prisms A–D showing white light entering and splitting into red and violet rays in different paths and exit positions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-science-combined-science-23-physics/waves/light/assets/001-four-labelled-glass-prisms-a-d-showing-white-lig.png)
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Violet light has a shorter wavelength than red light, so it is refracted more as it passes through the prism
- Red light is refracted the least; violet light is refracted the most

parts.problemMd: What is the frequency range of ultrasound?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- Ultrasound is sound with a frequency above 20 kHz, which is above the upper limit of human hearing
- The human audible range is 20 Hz to 20 kHz
